status: partial implementation, local checks passed; not versioned or published as 1.71
scope: Share the existing exact-case login and registration account retry policies across fresh connections, using bounded fixed-size hashed keys rather than trusted-looking client forwarding headers.
Bound simultaneous credential queries and password hashes to four by default, with an operator flag limited to 1-32. Reject excess work with retry feedback instead of an unbounded queue.
Return hash-work capacity before hydration, journals and takeover; release is idempotent and also deferred for exceptional exits.
Keep the per-connection protocol budget and use the same deterministic refill rule for both layers. Busy rejections do not consume an account retry.

checks.focusedRace: Credential, auth-dispatch, reconnect-token, closure-clock, queue, character-owner, session-activity, admin-admission and inbound-policy tests passed in 2.351 seconds after the final mixed-kind busy fixture enhancement. Earlier 2.537-second coverage overlaps and is not additive.
checks.actualSockets: TestCredentialActualFreshConnectionsAndTakeover passed against the production race-instrumented server binary and owned loopback Mongo in 10.06 seconds (package 11.110 seconds). Real bcrypt and normal messages prove legacy short-password login, account-switch refusal, fresh-socket five-attempt login/registration budgets, correct-password takeover/rotation, rejection of old and still-live bearer tokens, normal Fighter join despite the exhausted login budget, independent new registration/login from the same address, disconnect resume retaining the unburned token, and one-use revocation. No QA command or accelerated clock was used.

Read-only docker compose config with the sample environment and --no-env-resolution --quiet passed. The same built server rejected -1, 0 and 33 with exit2 before logging/database setup, using an unreachable loopback URI to prove fail-fast validation. No deployed environment or service was changed.
cases: Six fresh connections cannot exceed five same-account login attempts or five registration attempts; the next attempt refills after twelve seconds.
Held work bounds new login/registration admission; busy requests do not retain extra keys or consume their retry allowance.
One hundred distinct synthetic account names, case-sensitive names, Unicode identifiers and the separate registration/login policies remain independent. This is not a connected capacity load test.
A bounded map refuses new keys at capacity, releases rejected work slots and reclaims fully refilled entries on a one-minute sweep.
Clock rewind cannot replenish attempts; sixty-four concurrent same-account contenders have exactly five admitted attempts.
Repeated release is safe, and non-credential messages do not occupy hash-work capacity.
Actual login/registration dispatcher rejection occurs before the intentionally absent database for both busy and rate-limited cases.
checks.productionMutations: None; no production login, password reset, administrator mutation or database write was performed.

limits: RAM-only per-process budgets reset on restart; this is not a distributed edge limiter or a blanket denial-of-service solution.

A targeted account can still experience temporary denial while an attacker spends its refilling attempts. The operator guide records this, map saturation and the lack of a simultaneous100-player admission proof.

New-registration credential requirements, recovery ownership/delivery and complete administrator threat review remain unfinished milestone work. The connected proof is this bounded scenario, not a long-session, all-account, physical-phone or production acceptance claim.
No minimum password rule, saved-account migration, password logging, forwarding-header trust or recovery bypass was introduced.
1.63 is in deployment; 1.64-1.70 remain prepared and unpublished pending ordered acceptance.
